implementation_statement: Remote management of the router is through a VPN on the router. Since 2026-07-23 the router's web and SSH management no longer answer from the internet. Gap: management still answers on the subscriber-facing interfaces until the filter rework on 2026-09-15, and the consultant's VPN sessions are not logged or approved per session.

The owner has had no security or CPNI training. The owner will take a short CPNI compliance course from a WISP trade group or counsel and a basic security awareness course, and subscribe to monthly security bulletins, by 2026-11-30.

POL-01 4.5 requires review by someone outside the company, such as the network consultant, at least every second year. The billing vendor's SOC 2 Type 2 report, reviewed in P09, covers that vendor's inherited controls. Gap: the first outside review is planned for July 2027.
evidence: P07 assessment plan; POL-01 4.5; P09 vendor review

implementation_statement: The cloud radio controller holds the configuration of every access point and customer radio (inherited). Gap: there is no documented baseline for the edge router and core switch; the last configuration copy is 4 months old.
evidence: Controller configuration history; router configuration export

implementation_statement: Compensating control (one-person business): there is no change board, so under CM-3(g) the owner is the change control element. POL-01 9.4 requires every router and switch configuration change to go in the change log with the date and reason, and radio settings come from controller templates, so the cloud radio controller keeps their history. POL-01 7.3 requires vendor-default passwords and SNMP community strings to be changed before a device carries customer traffic. Gap: the change log and firmware deadlines are new under POAM-002, and the last router configuration copy is 4 months old.
evidence: POL-01 7.3 and 9.4; change log; controller configuration history; POAM-002

implementation_statement: Customer radios are set from a controller template. Gap: no written hardening settings for the router, switch, and access points. P07 found one SITE-3 access point with the vendor-default local password and SNMP community string.

The BIA (P05), POL-01 section 11, and the P08 runbook form the contingency plan. Gap: the sealed emergency access envelope and the standby agreement with the network consultant are not in place yet (due 2026-12-31).

Gap: MFA is offered but off on the VoIP reseller portal, which holds call detail for all 58 lines; router admin access uses a password over the VPN. The owner turns on portal MFA by 2026-09-15.
evidence: Account security pages; P07 sign-in test

implementation_statement: SaaS passwords are unique. Gap: passwords are stored in the laptop browser; every access point shares one local password; one access point still had the vendor-default password (changed 2026-07-23). The owner moves to a password manager and unique device passwords by 2026-10-31.

Customers set portal passwords through a link to the email of record, without biographical or account prompts (47 CFR 64.2010(c), (e)). Call detail by phone is given only by calling back the number of record or emailing the address of record (64.2010(b)). Gap: the AI support assistant on the text line accepted account number and service ZIP code before showing call history; that skill was turned off on 2026-07-22. Account change notices go out only for password changes (64.2010(f)).

The P08 notification matrix (adopted 2026-08-31) lists the CPNI law enforcement notice through the FCC reporting facility within 7 business days and the CALEA compromise report. Gap: the owner has not yet located the reporting facility link or the local FBI field office and USSS contacts (due 2026-09-30).
The network intrusion runbook (P08) was adopted on 2026-08-31. Gap: contacts not yet printed and the runbook has not been walked through with the network consultant (due 2026-09-30).
The SITE-1 shed is locked and alarmed to the owner's phone; tower bases are fenced. At leased sites the equipment cabinets are locked and the landlords control site access.
evidence: Walkthrough of SITE-1 and SITE-3 on 2026-07-21; site leases

implementation_statement: First risk assessment completed 2026-07-24 using SP 800-30 Rev. 1 (P01). Reviewed each July and after a major change.

No vulnerability scanning or advisory tracking today. From 2026-10 the owner subscribes to the router and radio vendors' security advisories and to the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog alerts, and runs a monthly external port check of the network's public addresses.
evidence: Advisory subscriptions and port check log (planned)

implementation_statement: The billing vendor, VoIP platform, radio vendor, and email provider operate under their service terms. The network consultant signed confidentiality and security terms on 2026-07-17. Gap: no written terms with the tower contractor; the VoIP provider's security was never reviewed; the AI support assistant was turned on without a review.

Access point management sits on its own VLAN, and since 2026-07-23 router management is blocked from the internet. Gap: router management still answers on subscriber-facing interfaces until 2026-09-15, and the owner's laptop sits on the same network as the management VLAN when at home.
evidence: Router filter rules; external port check

implementation_statement: SaaS sessions use TLS (inherited) and router management uses the VPN. Gap: the ATAs send call signaling and audio to the VoIP platform unencrypted; the platform supports encrypted signaling and media. Owner turns it on for all ATAs by 2026-12-31.

The laptop has full-disk encryption and the phone is encrypted by its passcode. The SaaS vendors encrypt stored data (billing vendor confirmed in its SOC 2 report). Retention of CDR exports on the laptop is handled under POL-01 8.4.

SaaS vendors patch their services; laptop and phone update automatically; the radio controller can push radio firmware. Gap: the edge router is two releases behind a vendor advisory rated critical (update set for 2026-09-15), and there is no schedule for router, switch, and access point firmware.
The laptop's built-in antivirus runs real-time scanning with automatic updates. Owner responsibility: keep it on and act on alerts.
